steps.content: "Please... believe me!"
Wendy looks at this person who, though injured, is continuing to embrace her. She slowly puts down her weapon.
Seeing Wendy's expression turn calm, you take her to a secluded area to rest a while.
Meanwhile, you begin to attempt to reestablish your comms.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, are you all right?
Yes, everything's fine.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Our monitoring data is showing that you’re bleeding from your shoulder and the Sinister Singularity’s emotional state reached a tipping point. You call that "everything’s fine"?
Listen to me, Nightingale. It wasn't Wendy's fault, and I'm fine.
You briefly and precisely summarize everything that just happened. Nightingale is silent for a while, then grants you permission to question Wendy alone outside.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I understand the situation. The support squad will set off right away to collect the two individuals you captured.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: She has an in-depth understanding of the Rust and she’s agile in combat... You should know that, while S-084 has been cleared of suspicion with regards to this incident, her mental state remains unstable. She’s dangerous, Chief.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...I understand. I’ll switch off the monitoring equipment, but if anything happens, contact me immediately.
When you return to Wendy's side, she's sitting on the ground in silence. Her hands and face are sticky with blood and her face looks expressionless—rather like an undertaker indeed.
Wendy doesn't respond, but quietly nods.
Wendy, you and your companions are stopping the spread of Corruptors, aren't you?
You can see that, rather than trading in cadavers, Wendy is the one trying to resolve the matter, and that the Undertakers weren't a dissident group, but rather a secret contamination cleanup squad.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Hah... You’re only just realizing this now?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: That’s right, I’m an Undertaker.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: This is everything I believe in.
You're the Undertaker who stayed true to your beliefs.
But I'd just like to know more about you... and your truth.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: My truth... Everything you see now is the truth!
I only see you right now, Wendy.
Would you be willing to tell me some more stories from back then?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Why... are you so interested in me?
I think it's one of the steps required to become a trustworthy companion.
Perhaps moved once again by this word, Wendy fell silent for a while, lingering in the conciliation, before speaking in a faint voice.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I was an orphan, and that person adopted me. I was bound to become an Undertaker...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: There, everyone was the same—We were all people with no future.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Our clothes were ragged... and we were injured but didn’t have any medicine. Once our wounds were exposed to the contamination, they gnawed away at us little by little...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: We lived each day under threat by monsters, and... the contamination, the crazy thoughts...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Yes, that’s it... Our job was to clean up the filth, so much filth, day in and day out. Over time, our vision got blurry and there were people talking nonstop in our heads...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I even wondered... if I wasn’t also just a monster with a sword hanging over my head... Haha... We’d go crazy sooner or later...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: But... everyone said it’s fine...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: They said that, since the contamination had taken everything from us, we couldn’t allow it to take away more people’s happiness.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Since there was nothing left to take from us, we were the best people for this great task.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: They said... since we’d found such a great task, we—these dead folk walking—had found a reason to live...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: See, aren’t they just the noblest, greatest people in the world?
Wendy smiles slightly. It's a gentle smile, but also a profoundly sad one.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: The captain... once said this to me...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: He said that our sacrifice was worth something, that people would thank us... that we would be remembered as heroes of the DisCity...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Haha... Idiot... What good are other people’s thanks...? Isn’t having each other enough?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: What do people in high places know about danger? What do they know about contamination?!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Those thieves, too... Dirty, vile... We were doing it to fight the contamination, we didn’t want their filthy money! Or those hypocritical thank-yous!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: But the captain betrayed us all, all for those insignificant nobodies...
Wendy chokes up slightly again, but stubbornly continues speaking.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: It was too cruel for him...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: That little boy... His eyes were red and streaming with tears before he was taken away... but he couldn't stop... laughing like a crazy person.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I asked him, that man, the captain...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: He said there was nothing we could do, not anything. "The people above" wouldn't allow it.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I wanted to know why "the people above" couldn’t protect him, couldn’t protect us!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: That’s why I followed him that day, to get a clear answer.
Wendy looks towards the person collapsed on the ground, her words bristling with indignation.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I learned from their conversation that, to the top, we're not even worth mentioning... We were always meant to die out here.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: We’re just scum with no way out! They can get as many maggots like us as they like!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Once one batch is all used up, they can just move on to the next one! There’s no need to give them good equipment!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: We’re the ones with the responsibility, we’re the ones who face the danger... but those dirtbags?!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Those dirtbags, they’re just more trash in this polluting stream of filth, there’s nothing human about them!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I'll chop off their fat-filled heads! While I still have breath... I'll split their necks open!
The tears that have been gathering in Wendy's eyes roll down her face and plummet to the ground.
Through gritted teeth, she denounces the forces responsible for her tragic past. It's heartbreaking to listen to.
You hold her hand and gently place it over your heart, hoping she can feel it beat.
Thank you for trusting me enough to tell me this. I believe you, Wendy.
I'm sorry for making you think about such awful things... I'm going to help prove your and your companions' innocence.
So, can you let me meet your companions?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: My companions... What are you gonna do to them?!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Lock them up, put them in chains, and throw them into danger again?!
No, Wendy, definitely not...
None of you were traitors to the organization, on the contrary, you paid a huge price on its behalf.
I won't let you all stay buried here like this.
I have a duty to fight for the innocence you deserve.
Consider it a thank-you... to you and your comrades for fighting for the light in this world.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: But... can I trust you all?
After hearing this, Wendy is silent for a long time. Finally, she bursts into loud laughter, as if having just heard a joke.
She takes you by the hand and leads you to that piece of earth in the morning sun.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Hahahaha...!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I was wrong, Mister Chief.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I’ll take you... to see my comrades, Chief.
Wendy takes your hand and leads you straight ahead. You realize that you're headed "south" like those two body brokers mentioned.
You pass through the stench of rotting corpses and finally arrive at a quiet clearing.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: We’re here...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Nova? John? Are you guys awake?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Ah... Sorry, Chief. They’re still sleeping, so they’re not ready to see you yet. Come in, we can wait for them to get up together.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Welcome to the house of the Undertakers.
She speaks in an exceptionally gentle voice, but no one comes out to greet you from the place she calls home.
In the bright red sunlight, you can clearly see that several holes have been dug in this place before hastily being filled back up...
Strange things have been placed in front of the pits, as if they were nestled up together in a peaceful slumber.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Come in, come in, just... keep your voice down a little...
Wendy's voice lowers as she raises a finger over her pursed lips.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: They’re tired, we should let them sleep.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I’ll introduce you to all of them—quietly, of course.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: This is Nova, he’s a big goofball. It’s almost impossible to move him once he’s gone to sleep, even though we clearly eat the same things every day.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: And this one, the one I set with stones!
Wendy points to a different pit, atop of which is strewn several small stones commonly found by the Rust.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: This is John, he’s an orphan who can’t even count, but he can clearly remember how many Corruptors he buried.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: For everyone he buried, he would find a stone to remember it by and carry it with him... I put all those stones next to his pillow!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: But he asked me to add one more stone this time. He said that when he turns into a Corruptor completely, he’ll bury himself...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: But I didn’t add it. Since he’s so tired, he won’t notice if it’s there or not while he’s sleeping.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Then there’s her... My poor Lily...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: She’s Fino’s good friend, but she could only watch as Fino mutated little by little... there was nothing we could do. In the end, we buried Fino together...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: It wasn’t easy getting her to fall asleep, so make sure you don’t wake her up. Otherwise, she’ll start crying again.
Wendy gently pats the pit, as if lulling a child to sleep.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: As for me... This is my bed here!
She points to a newly-dug shallow pit at the end of the row of graves, then lies down in it, curling up and smiling at you.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I sleep here every day together with everyone else. Too bad they’re always sleeping in, I’m the only one who ever gets up.
Wendy... you can't sleep with them...
They're... already dead.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: They’re... They’re dead?!
I'm sorry, Wendy.
Those people already have their eyes on this place, these bodies can't stay here anymore.
The best thing we can do for them is taking them away from here...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Why would you say that they’re dead...? Why do you want to take them away...?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Those traitors said the same thing... Do you want their bodies, too?!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: They’re not dead! They’ll never leave me!!
Wendy breaks down again and her eyes look so red that blood could drip out of them.
She cries, laughs, and snarls at you.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Hahahaha! I knew it, you FAC dog!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: You’re just like them! Trampling on us!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I know all about your depraved ideas!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: But one day... you’ll be just like the Undertakers were back then!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Betrayed by your loved ones... Betrayed by everyone!!!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: You’ll see everyone die right before your eyes...

options: Apologize to Wendy and reassure her

choices.text: Apologize to Wendy and reassure her

steps.content: I'm sorry, Wendy. I don't want to separate you and your companions whatsoever.
Ignoring the chainsaw pointed at you, you slowly walk forward and hold her hand.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: You’re no companion of mine, don’t touch me...
But I can't leave you here all alone.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: What are you talking about? Everyone’s right here with me. The Undertakers will be together forever.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I want to wait for them to wake up...
You already know this, don't you...

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Shut up!
She shouts this angrily, but her gradually reddening eyes avoid your gaze, as if she is trying hard to resist something.
You look at the pit where she "sleeps peacefully every night".

options: That's the grave you dug for yourself, isn't it?

choices.text: That's the grave you dug for yourself, isn't it?

steps.content: You remembered the day that each of them left and gave them a comfortable final resting place. You gave them all a warm burial.
But Wendy, now that you've seen everyone off, who will lay you to rest?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Ooohhh... Waaahhhhh!!!
Her suppressed choking sobs finally burst into cries of grief. Her chainsaw drops into the mud, and the last Undertaker falls to her knees, trembling.
You lean down and gently cup her face, wiping away her endless stream of tears.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I’m the last one, there won’t be any new Undertakers in this world again. This will all end here with me, I swear it!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: If they were still here, I could go on shouldering the burden of the undertakers... but those scumbags want their remains...!!

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I just want them!
You take her into your arms. The scent of the soil from the grave has dispelled the smell of blood from her body, like opening a room that has been shut for a long time.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Let them stay with me, don’t take them away from me... please.
Someday, if you also... want to sleep, I'll take you to be with them... I can promise you that much.
But you're still alive right now... You're still a human being, Wendy. While you're alive, why don't you stay with me?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: ...Why?
Because I'm just like you, I can't bear the pain of losing people close to me.
If I die, how will you feel?

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: No, I don’t want you to die. I won’t allow it.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: I won’t bury you. If you die... I’ll really have nothing left... So, you’re not allowed to die!
Okay... I'll do my best. Thanks for letting me be your companion.
Since you're carrying the burden of the Undertakers, then until the day you return to their side...

options: Let me carry it with you.

choices.text: Let me carry it with you.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Okay... I promise, too.

steps.speaker: Wendy
steps.content: Before they come to take me home, you’ll... be my home.
Her voice grows smaller and smaller as she slowly closes her eyes. After a long and exhausting night, she drifts off to sleep in your arms.
Did you save her?
You don't know.
But at the very least, tonight she won't have to sleep on a pillow of death in that small, cold pit.
